subject: physics
question_text: State the two conditions under which Bernoulli's theorem can be applied.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Mechanical Properties of Fluids, Very Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Bernoulli's theorem is derived for the steady, streamline flow of a fluid that is non-viscous, so no energy is lost to internal friction between its layers, and incompressible, so its density is the same at every point — both are needed for the sum of pressure, kinetic and potential energy per unit mass to stay constant along a streamline.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Non-viscous — no friction losses
steps.mark_note: Non-viscous: no energy lost to friction
lines: The first condition is that the
No energy is then lost to
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name non-viscous and say why: no energy lost to friction.
steps.why: Without this condition, some of the fluid's mechanical energy would be lost to internal friction as it flows, and the sum would fall rather than stay constant.
common_mistakes: Naming non-viscous without saying what it means for the energy — that no energy is lost to friction.
Confusing non-viscous with incompressible. Non-viscous is about friction between layers, not density.

recall.must_convey: That the fluid must be non-viscous, so no energy is lost to internal friction as it flows.

steps.memory_tip: Non-viscous means no friction, so no energy is lost.

steps.label: Incompressible — fixed density
lines: The second condition is that the
density stays the same at every
This lets the same density ρ be
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name incompressible and say why: one fixed density ρ.
steps.why: If the density changed from point to point, a single ρ could not stand for the whole flow, and the formula would need a different ρ at each point.
common_mistakes: Naming incompressible without saying that the density is the same at every point.
Giving steady flow and only one other condition. Steady flow is assumed as well, but the two conditions this question asks for are non-viscous and incompressible.

recall.must_convey: That the fluid must be incompressible, so its density is the same at every point.

steps.memory_tip: Incompressible means one fixed ρ for the whole flow.

insider_note: Two marks, two named conditions: non-viscous and incompressible. Steady flow is the setting Bernoulli's theorem is derived in, not one of the two conditions asked for.
